title: Working at Redwood: Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Tools
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

This document consolidates the primary company-handbook items new and existing Redwood Inference employees reference daily: what it’s like to work here, our role and career ladder structure, benefits and perks, hiring and onboarding process, and the core internal tools and access patterns. Use the links in Related pages for role-specific and team-specific detail.

## Working at Redwood — culture & expectations

- Mission alignment: We build and operate inference infrastructure that helps engineering teams ship reliable LLM features. Employees are expected to prioritize operational excellence, customer impact, and measurable cost/latency outcomes.
- Ways we work: asynchronous-first communication, distributed teams with regular face-to-face (onsite) cadences, and a bias toward ownership and measurable outcomes.
- Inclusion and conduct: Redwood requires inclusive behaviors. See the People Ops Code of Conduct page for reporting and escalation steps (link in Related pages).
- Work model: remote-first with regional hubs. Individual roles may specify required days in-office; team leads publish yearly onsite plans.

## Roles & career ladders (high-level)

This section summarizes typical ladders for cross-functional disciplines. Each team maintains a detailed ladder document aligned to this canonical map. Levels and titles may differ slightly between functions; compensation bands are managed separately by Total Rewards.

Eng & Applied ML (individual contributor focus)
- E1 (New grad / Junior Eng): follows direction, contributes to small components.
- E2 (SWE / ML Engineer): owns features, independent delivery on routine scope.
- E3 (Senior): owns services, mentors peers, drives non-trivial designs.
- E4 (Staff): cross-team impact, technical leadership over a domain, sets standards.
- E5 (Principal / Distinguished IC): company-level strategy, leads major technical initiatives and public-facing benchmarks.

Engineering Management
- M1 (Eng Manager): manages 1–3 teams or 6–10 engineers, execution and career growth of direct reports.
- M2 (Senior Manager): owns a larger area, managers-of-managers, cross-functional delivery.
- M3 (Director): org strategy, budgeting and cross-org alignment.

Product & Design
- P1 (Associate PM / Designer) → P2 (PM / Product Designer) → P3 (Senior) → P4 (Lead / Staff) → P5 (Director/Group PM)

Customer Success, Sales, GTM
- C1/C2: Individual contributors, account or AE level → C3 (Senior) → C4 (Lead) → C5 (Head of function)

Promotion criteria (summary)
- Clear scope of ownership and measurable outcomes.
- Demonstrated increase in complexity and cross-team influence.
- Consistent performance evidence from past 6–12 months and manager + peer feedback.
- For managers: evidence of developing others and expanding team outcomes.

For full criteria and calibration process see the team-specific Career-Ladders documents (owners: People Ops + Hiring managers).

## Benefits & perks (summary)

- Health & wellbeing
  - Medical, dental, and vision plans with company coverage tiers (primary, family). Plan details and vendors available on the Benefits portal.
  - Mental health: EAP + 10 therapy sessions reimbursed per year.
- Financial benefits
  - Competitive salary bands, annual performance review cycles, and equity grants for full-time employees.
  - 401(k) plan with company match (US). Country-specific retirement options for international employees.
- Time off and leave
  - Flexible PTO policy: target 20 days PTO/year for full-time employees; encourages taking regular breaks.
  - Parental leave: 16 weeks primary caregiver, 8 weeks secondary caregiver (paid).
  - Caregiver and family support allowance for adoption/fertility assistance.
- Learning & development
  - $2,000 annual learning stipend (conference, courses, books).
  - Quarterly internal tech talks, mentorship program, and manager 1:1 guidelines.
- Work experience & home office
  - Home office stipend on hire and every 24 months. Regional co-working and relocation support options exist for hires who need them.
- Perks
  - Commuter stipends where applicable, monthly wellness reimbursement, team offsites budget, and equity refresh cycles for high-impact contributors.

Policy references: full legal plan documents live on the Benefits portal and payroll pages (People Ops owner).

## Hiring & onboarding — process overview

1. Hiring pipeline (high level)
   1. Requisition created and approved by hiring manager + People Ops.
   2. Sourcing & screening: Recruiter screens for role fit and coordinates technical screens.
   3. Interview loop: typically includes hiring manager screen, two technical interviews (coding/architecture or product), an onsite or virtual loop with cross-functional interviews, and a final bar-raiser/peer review.
   4. Offer & checks: People Ops extends offers, manages reference checks and background checks where required.
   5. Offer acceptance & scheduling: Recruiter coordinates start date, relocation and remote onboarding logistics.

2. Typical interview loop for Eng (example)
   - Recruiter screen (30 min)
   - Hiring manager (45 min): role expectations and fit
   - System design or ML architecture (60 min)
   - Coding / implementation (60 min)
   - Cross-functional collaboration (product or SRE) (45 min)
   - Panel / bar-raiser (30–45 min)

3. Onboarding: first 90 days (owner: People Ops + Hiring manager)
   - Pre-start (Recruiter): account setup checklist, laptop shipping, workspace stipend, welcome packet.
   - Day 0–7: Admin tasks, benefits enrollment, security training, manager 1:1, team intro.
   - Week 2–4: Project onboarding, first contribution (bugfix or small feature), mentor assignment.
   - Month 1: 30-day check-in (manager), goal alignment, training plan established.
   - Month 2: broader org introductions, ownership on a feature, feedback cycle started.
   - Month 3: 90-day review, performance calibration if needed, continued career-path conversation.

Onboarding checklist (select items)
- Accounts & access: Okta SSO, GitHub org access, Slack, Jira, Confluence, Google Workspace, internal CI/CD access.
- Security & compliance training: required module completion within first week.
- Payroll & benefits: complete forms and elections before pay cycle.
- Hardware & dev setup: laptop imaged, dev container or cloud sandbox access documented in Eng Dev Quickstarts.

## Internal tools & quick guides

- Communication
  - Slack: engineering channels (#eng-runtime, #eng-infra, #oncall), policy for public channels, and guidelines for escalation. Use DND for focus time and set status during deep work.
  - All-hands & town halls scheduled monthly; recordings and notes posted to Confluence.
- Identity & access
  - Okta: primary SSO provider. New hires receive activation email from okta-admin@redwood.ai. Use multi-factor authentication (MFA) – required.
  - Access requests: use the Access Request form (link in Related pages). For elevated infra access open an RFC with Eng Security.
- Code & release
  - GitHub: repo structure is org-level. Main branches follow trunk-based development. See the Dev Branching and PR standards doc.
  - CI/CD: builds run in the shared CI project. For private deploys, see eng-private-deployments reference architecture for packaging and air-gap steps.
- Ticketing & planning
  - Jira: sprint planning cadence is 2 weeks. Tickets require clear definitions of done and linked PRs.
  - Confluence: canonical home for runbooks, PRDs, and design docs. Use the company template when creating new pages.
- Observability & incident response
  - Dashboards: core dashboards in Eng Platform; alert owners are listed in the Dashboards & Alerts page.
  - Oncall: follow the Oncall and Incident Response runbook for escalation and postmortems.
- Expenses & procurement
  - Use Expensify for local expenses and the Procurement Request form for vendor purchases > $5,000.
